comparison: Perfect alignment on computational modeling claims (C70-C74). Both evaluations support the docking analysis and mechanistic insights. Peer review notes this computational work was added in revision and strengthens the manuscript, while OpenEval acknowledges limitations regarding closed-state modeling.

Strong agreement on biophysical characterization of RY785-resistant currents (C34-C38). Both evaluations support these findings without critique. OpenEval emphasizes consistency with prior literature (Salinas et al., 1997a), while peer review implicitly accepts the evidence as part of the effective breakdown of a complex problem.

Both evaluations support foundational background claims (C1-C2, C9-C12) about KvS proteins. OpenEval characterizes these as well-established facts from prior literature providing context, while peer review treats them as accepted knowledge without questioning the background.

Strong agreement on SCG neuron data (C45-C49) showing predominantly RY785-sensitive currents. Both evaluations support these findings. Peer review treats SCG as a negative control demonstrating predominantly homomeric channels, while OpenEval notes the small remaining current (12%) attributed to non-Kv2 channels.

Both evaluations support human DRG neuron findings (C63-C65). OpenEval notes lack of significant difference between RY785 and vehicle controls but maintains support based on biophysical properties. Peer review accepts these data without critique, emphasizing translational relevance.

Strong agreement on mouse DRG neuron data (C54-C60) demonstrating RY785-resistant, GxTX-sensitive conductances. Both evaluations strongly support these findings as key demonstrations of the method's utility in physiologically relevant neurons expressing functional Kv2/KvS heteromers.

Both evaluations strongly support the core finding (C4, C5, C66-C67) that RY785 and GxTX can distinguish Kv2/KvS heteromers from homomers. OpenEval provides detailed technical validation across multiple figures, while peer review emphasizes this as a significant advance with compelling experimental evidence.

Overlap on heterologous expression data (C24-C27). OpenEval's R1 covers these claims as part of comprehensive pharmacological validation, while peer R2 specifically addresses heterologous expression foundations. Both evaluations support the data without questioning the approach.

Overlap on pharmacological characterization (C28-C33, C69). OpenEval's R1 includes these as part of comprehensive differential pharmacology demonstration, while peer R3 specifically addresses dose-response and kinetic data. Both evaluations accept the pharmacological strategy as robust.

Overlap on generalizability across KvS subtypes (C39-C40, C42, C68). OpenEval's R1 includes these in comprehensive validation, while peer R5 specifically emphasizes this as a key strength allowing identification of heteromers containing any of 10 mammalian KvS subunits.

Partial overlap on study rationale and methodological contribution (C14-C15, C80). OpenEval R8 addresses background rationale from prior literature, while OpenEval R12 addresses C80 as a conclusion. Peer R10 emphasizes the methodological advance addressing a longstanding roadblock in the field.

Overlap on background context (C3, C8, C13). OpenEval R8 addresses rationale and state of the field from prior literature, while peer R11 covers broader foundational background. Both evaluations treat these as established knowledge supporting the study's motivation.

Both address the methodological contribution and implications (C80). OpenEval characterizes C80 as a direct conclusion from pharmacological characterization and C82 as appropriately qualified speculation. Peer review strongly affirms the methodological advance and its potential impact.

Minimal overlap on C41 regarding surface localization. OpenEval R10 specifically validates transfected KvS subunits form functional heteromers with immunofluorescence and functional data. Peer R5 focuses on generalizability across KvS subtypes without specifically addressing surface localization validation.
